findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context builds a display-friendly config copy but returns the original
findings.body: The function copies `monitor.config` and replaces `schedule_type` with `get_schedule_type_display()`. It then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the uncopied original) under "config", so the copy is dead code. The event's `contexts.monitor.config` therefore carries the raw numeric `schedule_type` instead of the human-readable value. The bug came over with the move. Since the code now lives in a new module, it is a good moment to return `config` instead.

findings.title: get_failure_reason produces a malformed message when no statuses match the map
findings.body: `status_counts` only counts check-ins whose status is in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP` (ERROR, MISSED, TIMEOUT). If none match, `sum(...)` is 0 and the singular branch is skipped. `get_text_list([])` then returns an empty string, and the result is " check-ins detected" with a leading space and no count. This can happen when `previous_checkins` contains only other statuses. That list comes from the last N check-ins ordered by `date_added`, so for example an in-progress check-in is not filtered out. The evidence value shown to users would then be garbage. A fallback message for the empty case would avoid it.
